question: Does requiring corroborating consecutive feedback errors prevent gratuitous model switches under isolated corrupted feedback, and what adaptation delay does it impose during a true hidden operation change?
world: Fresh seeds208..215 (development208..211, heldout212..215),16 contexts/episodes, second-order ADD4 and XOR4 with hidden four-symbol observation permutation SHA256('W34-perm/'+seed) byte0 mod24 and unique SHA256('W34-order/'+seed+'/'+episode) context presentation order. Odd seeds remain ADD4. Even seeds switch from ADD4 to XOR4 for t>=16; no regime flag reaches learners. 16 t2 labeled calibration contexts permit unique ADD and XOR predictive tables within fixed W26 24 permutations or experiment is AMBIGUOUS. Evaluation always uses exact latent-generated true target, but the learner's distinct supervisory feedback report is corrupted by +1 modulo4 at ticks7 and24 of every episode, selected in advance; t+1 context is provided via a distinct uncorrupted state-observation channel. These two channels and the evaluator-only truth are explicit.
arms: FROZEN_ADD uses calibrated ADD table forever, ignores supervisor feedback
ONE_ERROR_TOGGLE starts in ADD and toggles ADD/XOR after every observed prediction-vs-reported-feedback disagreement, taking effect on next tick
TWO_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS starts ADD and toggles only after two consecutive disagreements with reported feedback, takes effect next tick and clears mismatch count; any agreement resets count.
budget: 16 supervised calibration labels for each seed, 16 episodes x29 forecasts at t3..31 per seed; all arms same 2 precommitted corrupt postforecast reports per episode. No further labeled calibration beyond supervised reports observed AFTER each forecast; no actual evaluation truth visible to learner except separate clean two-value context at next tick. Both candidate tables fixed before evaluation.
metrics: All8 raw observed full trajectory fingerprint SHA256 distinct excluding seed name; calibration uniqueness for both ADD and XOR predictive tables; heldout STABLE/SHIFT accuracy vs ground truth (not corrupted feedback), number of toggles in each phase, pre t3..15 and post t16..31 correct/wrong, first switch delay, trace SHA256, corrupt supervision count exactly 2/episode.
frozen_classification: NOISE_HYSTERESIS_TRADEOFF if calibration/source valid, heldout STABLE TWO_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS makes fewer wrong forecasts and fewer toggles than ONE_ERROR_TOGGLE, but heldout SHIFT TWO_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS does not exceed ONE_ERROR_TOGGLE in correct post-t16 forecasts. MIXED otherwise. INVALID_IDENTITIES or AMBIGUOUS_HYPOTHESIS for guard failures.
safeguards: Frozen before source and first use, original Git SHA pins for W26/prereg/evaluator, no candidate expansion, no post-result threshold tuning, no first-use retry, original science JSON and full Go test/build. Keep all negatives, mixed, invalid. No model calls, live activation, accepted-reference mutation.
claim_limit: Fixed synthetic two-operation and precommitted noisy supervisor with a separate perfect context channel; not unconstrained error recovery or safe learning under general noise.
